name: NeuralPath Cascade Standard Feed BCI
description:
The NeuralPath Cascade Standard Feed is a full-spectrum consumer neural mesh designed for reliable, low-latency feed access across GLMZ's civic and commercial networks. Installed via a 45-minute outpatient procedure, it integrates six cortical contact points and a subdural antenna array to deliver persistent AR overlay, real-time messaging, payment authorization, and civic identity verification. Its bandwidth of 4.2 Gbps neural throughput is sufficient for simultaneous AR navigation, social feed streaming, and workplace data terminals without perceptible lag, making it the most purchased BCI in the Tier 2 market for three consecutive years.

The Cascade is the BCI you see on every transit worker, warehouse crew chief, and corner-shop owner in the Shelf's upper blocks and the Tier 2 corridors. It lacks the aesthetic polish of SynapTech products or the performance ceiling of CortexDynamics hardware, but it simply works — day after day, firmware update after firmware update, without drama. NeuralPath's service network is the largest in GLMZ, with certified recalibration kiosks in most mid-tier pharmacies and transit hubs, meaning a broken Cascade rarely means a trip to a clinic. The unit carries a mild social stigma in Tier 4 and above, where it reads as working-class, but in Tiers 2-3 it is as unremarkable as shoes.
installation_requirements: Licensed outpatient clinic or certified pharmacy-grade installation booth; local anesthetic; 45-minute procedure
rejection_risk: Low — mature biocompatible polymer housing with 97.3% acceptance rate across tested demographics; antirejection firmware auto-adjusts neural contact pressure
maintenance: Automatic firmware updates pushed every 72 hours; manual recalibration recommended every 6 months at any NeuralPath kiosk; neural pathway diagnostics run passively in background

side_effects: Mild feed-bleed during sleep — AR elements occasionally intrude on dreaming in the first 3 months post-installation
Low-grade tinnitus-equivalent in 8% of users, described as a faint 'digital hum' that fades within 6 weeks
Occasional involuntary social-feed notifications causing micro-distraction during physical tasks
Headaches during firmware update cycles, typically lasting 2-4 hours
cultural_context: The Cascade is the BCI equivalent of a reliable mid-range work boot — respected by the people who wear it, invisible to everyone else. In Tier 2 communities it functions as a class marker in the most neutral sense: owning one means you are plugged in, employed, and credit-rated. Tier 3 professionals sometimes upgrade out of the Cascade to signal upward mobility, while Tier 4 residents would consider wearing one a step backward. On the Shelf, a working Cascade is aspirational; many Tier 1 residents carry grey-market or secondhand Cascades that have been reflashed to bypass subscription fees.

story_hooks: A routine NeuralPath firmware push contains an undocumented behavioral telemetry module — hundreds of thousands of Cascade users across GLMZ are unknowingly feeding location and purchasing data to an unknown third party. A player with a Cascade begins noticing irregularities in their own feed logs.

A Tier 1 fixer is running a brisk business reflashing stolen Cascades with cracked firmware that bypasses NeuralPath's subscription wall — but the latest batch of reflashed units is causing users to receive ghost signals from a decommissioned civic network node that was supposed to have gone dark years ago.

A NeuralPath recalibration kiosk in a Tier 2 transit hub has been physically tampered with — anyone who used it in the last 48 hours has had a passive surveillance codec inserted into their Cascade without their knowledge.
